paper_metadata.title: Microstructural stability and high-temperature mechanical properties of AZ91 and AZ91 + 2RE magnesium alloys

evidence.quote: The AZ91 alloy containing 9 wt.% Al and 1 wt.% Zn is the most commonly used cast magnesium alloy for low-temperature applications.
The addition of rare earth elements reﬁned the microstructure and improved both thermal stability and high-temperature mechanical properties of AZ91.

attributes.location: inside grains and grain boundary areas

evidence.quote: the thermally stable Al 11RE3 particles are distributed inside the grains as well as in the grain boundary areas.
the base AZ91 alloy exhibits a dendritic microstructure with some b-Mg17Al12 second phase particles distributed in the interdendritic regions
Addition of RE to the base alloy results in a change in both morphology and volume fraction of the particles, as shown in Fig. 1b.
after 4 h of annealing, the dendritic microstructure of AZ91 base alloy completely transforms to an equiaxed grain structure with an average grain size of about 150 lm.
The longer annealing time of 24 h, results in an even coarser structure with a grain size of about 600 lm (Fig. 3c).

The longer annealing time of 24 h, however, transforms the dendritic structure to a nearly equiaxed grain structure with a grain size of about 80 lm, which contains substantial amounts of particles inside the grains.

mechanisms.name: grain boundary sliding inhibition by thermally stable particles

evidence.quote: This is achieved by obstructing the dislocation annihilation and thus restricting the slip inside the grains, and also by inhibiting the grain boundary migration or grain boundary sliding during deformation.

Reﬁnement of the microstructure, hardening by the Al 11RE3 particles, and the high thermal stability of this phase, which can resist softening and dissolution during annealing treatments, are the main mechanisms responsible for the enhanced strength

Therefore, they strengthen both grains and grain boundaries and oppose both recovery and recrystallization processes during deformation at elevated temperatures, increasing the shear strength of the materials.

Higher strength of the 4 h-annealed condition in comparison with the as-cast state can be ascribed to the simultaneous effects of signiﬁcant solid solution hardening and elimination of the deteriorating role of Mg17Al12 at high temperatures.
it seems that the drop in strength due to excessive grain growth occurred in 24 h-annealed condition somehow diminishes the effect of these two microstructural features.

The fact that the strength of the as-cast condition shows a more pronounced drop with temperature may reﬂect the role of Mg17Al12 coarsening and softening in the weakening of the material at high temperatures.
